title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Mind-1: Physical AI framework cuts inference latency

### The Breakthrough
Mind-1 introduces a high‑precision data pipeline, a hierarchical control stack, and a custom FlashRT inference engine that together slash model inference latency from 82 ms to 32 ms (61% reduction) and halve end‑to‑end decision latency to 77.5 ms, enabling logistics‑task cycle times that match or exceed human speed on three robot embodiments.

### The Caveats
The work provides no comparison to external state‑of‑the‑art methods, so its claim of human‑level performance remains unverified.

## PRISM: Counterfactual video generation for humanoid loco‑manipulation

### The Breakthrough
PRISM expands a handful of real human‑object interaction videos into hundreds of counterfactual clips via video‑to‑video generation, reconstructs physically plausible trajectories, and trains a single policy that directly controls a real humanoid robot (depth‑only) to pick, carry, and drop diverse objects such as boxes and barrels.

### The Caveats
No baseline comparison to existing imitation or sim‑to‑real approaches is provided.

## Rho: Efficiently adaptable VLA models for dual‑arm manipulation

### The Breakthrough
Rho combines embodiment‑midtraining with a lightweight online adaptation module, achieving strong performance on three dual‑arm platforms (YAM Box, UR AI Trainer, FR3 Duo) with as few as 15 corrected episodes and matching or exceeding open‑weight VLA baselines.

### The Caveats
The baselines are unnamed, making it unclear how strong the reported improvements are.

## SimpleICL: Democratized in‑context robot learning

### The Breakthrough
SimpleICL defines a clear ICL problem, uses a visual prompt encoder and inexpensive data collection, and attains competitive results on both simulated and real‑world manipulation benchmarks without massive pretraining.

### The Caveats
The paper lacks comparison to existing ICL or large‑pretrained baselines.

## Skill‑Space Shooting for autonomous robot policy improvement

### The Breakthrough
The method treats corrective actions as sequences of reusable skills, steers a sampling process with a foundation model, and harvests successful roll‑outs as supervised data, enabling robots to iteratively refine policies and transfer skills to new tasks without human demonstrations.

### The Caveats
Improvements are shown only in ad‑hoc real‑world trials with no quantitative baseline.

## mesozoic‑labs: dinosaur‑inspired locomotion research platform

### The Breakthrough
The open‑source repo bundles articulated MJCF models, a curriculum manager, and Stable‑Baselines3/JAX pipelines to train RL agents on MuJoCo environments that simulate various dinosaurs and a crocodylomorph, facilitating unconventional locomotion studies.

### The Caveats
Results are limited to simulation and lack comparison to established RL baselines.

## China ships 19k humanoid robots H1 2026, 78% of global market

### The Breakthrough
IDC reports China shipped over 19,000 humanoid robots in H1 2026, accounting for 77.9% of global shipments; total global shipments rose ~432% YoY to ~25,000 units, with a forecast of >750,000 units by 2030.

### The Caveats
The figures rely solely on IDC data with no independent verification of robot capabilities or real‑world deployment.

### Priority
Mind-1’s dramatic latency reduction and demonstrated human‑speed cycle times across multiple robots make it the most immediately actionable advance for developers seeking faster embodied AI.

### One action
Explore Mind‑1’s open‑source inference engine (FlashRT) and benchmark its 32 ms latency on your own hardware.

### What to watch
Several stories target faster, more adaptable manipulation: Mind‑1 focuses on low‑latency inference, Rho on data‑efficient policy adaptation, PRISM on synthetic video data for sim‑to‑real transfer, SimpleICL on cheap in‑context learning, and Skill‑Space Shooting on autonomous skill composition. Together they signal a shift toward reducing engineering overhead while boosting real‑world performance.
